answer_1.quote: Automatically generating a presentation from a given multimodal document is challenging because of several reasons. Compared to a flat document summary, the slide narrative should convey a story to its audience and is often non-linear with respect to the flow of information in the document.
answer_1.outputs: slides with titles, bullet points, and images

answer_2.quote: We have carefully chosen three unsupervised metrics here: 1. Coverage: It is an unsupervised metric which intuitively capture how much does a subset "cover" the content of the super set. 2. Perplexity (PPL): Perplexity is a metric to indicate the fluency of the generated text. 3. LLM-Eval for presentation quality

answer_3.quote: We use LLM-Eval to measure the overall presentation quality in terms of organization, effectiveness, clarity, coherence, and the ability to convey complex ideas to the audience.

answer_4.quote: We have also conducted a small scale human survey to understand the quality of the generated presentation to human experts. First, we selected five research papers from ACL workshops which are relatively easy to follow. We hired two professional reviewers who have reasonable understanding of NLP and have good presentation generation skill.
answer_4.guideline: Based on our discussion with subject matter experts, we decided the following criteria to evaluate the quality of a generated presentation from a given document: (1) Readability: How good is the language and readability?, (2) Consistency: Is a slide title consistent with the slide content?, (3) Coverage: Does the presentation cover all important parts of the document?, (4) Diversity: Is the content of the presentation non-repetitive enough?, (5) Flow: How is the flow of information in the presentation? and (6) Usability: Is the generated presentation good enough for an initial draft?
